extracted.intended_audience: medical device manufacturers/applicants, hospital billing administrators, health policy stakeholders submitting comments to CMS
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and proposed approval criteria for CMS new technology add-on payments (NTAP) for FY 2027, including cost eligibility, coding, timing (newness) and documentation requirements for medical devices (including Breakthrough Devices). Intended to guide applicants and commenters on CMS's preliminary assessments and proposed payment amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost criterion for NTAP
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS evaluates whether a technology 'meets the cost criterion' as part of the NTAP approval decision (repeatedly stated: 'we agree with the applicant that [technology] meets the cost criterion and are therefore proposing to approve ... for new technology add-on payments for FY 2027').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS invites public comments on whether each device meets the cost criterion and on CMS's proposal to approve new technology add-on payments for FY 2027. CMS may update cost information in the final rule based on revised or additional information received prior to the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum NTAP payment calculation (65% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes the maximum new technology add-on payment for a case involving the use of a technology as '65% of the average cost of the technology' for FY 2027 (examples: dollar amounts provided for many devices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes that the cost information may be updated in the final rule. Also, per policy (§ 412.88(a)(2)), any NTAP is limited to the lesser of 65 percent of the average cost of the technology, or 65 percent of the costs in excess of the MS-DRG payment for the case; CMS will apply that limiting policy when determining final payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness period start date (beginning of newness period)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considers the beginning of the newness period to commence on the date on which the technology 'received FDA marketing authorization' or 'became commercially available' (examples: dates listed for each device).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses the marketing authorization/commercial availability date to determine the newness period relevant for NTAP eligibility; examples in the rule show dates used for multiple devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pathway limited to Breakthrough Device-designated indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the eligibility criteria for approval under the alternative pathway for certain transformative devices, 'only the use of the technology for the indication that corresponds to the technology's Breakthrough Device designation would be eligible for the new technology add-on payment for FY 2027.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a technology has other FDA approvals beyond its Breakthrough Device designation, only the Breakthrough-designated indication (and use cases corresponding to that indication) are relevant for NTAP eligibility. CMS gives an example where an indication (use in absence of fusion) was not included in the Breakthrough Device designation, therefore not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for FDA marketing authorization by specified date (time‑limited eligibility condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For several applications CMS conditions proposed approval 'subject to the technology receiving FDA marketing authorization for the indication corresponding to the Breakthrough Device designation by May 1, 2026.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will only approve NTAP for devices that receive FDA marketing authorization for the Breakthrough-designated indication by the specified cutoff date; multiple device entries reference this conditional requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICD-10-PCS procedure coding to identify NTAP-eligible use
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS identifies and believes certain ICD-10-PCS procedure codes would be 'appropriate to report in combination with use of the [technology] to identify use of the technology for the Breakthrough Device-designated indication' for purposes of NTAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides tables of relevant ICD-10-PCS procedure codes (and device-specific procedure codes where applicable) and explicitly invites public comments on the use of these codes to identify NTAP-eligible use. In some cases CMS notes newly effective custom codes (e.g., XW0U0XB, XW0U3XB, XW0U4XB) and the need to report codes in combination to uniquely describe procedures involving the technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of capital costs from NTAP (operating costs only)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS states that it 'does not include capital costs in the add-on payments for a new medical service or technology' and that NTAPs are not made under IPPS for capital-related costs; only operating costs are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites statute and prior rulemaking (e.g., section 1886(d)(5)(K)(i), 86 FR 45145, 72 FR 47307–47308) to justify excluding capital costs. Several device examples show capital components (e.g., TGFR Monitor, reusable sensors, PRU capital cost, capital portion of bone graft kit) treated as ineligible and NTAP amounts adjusted to reflect only operating costs. CMS requests additional information where a component appears reusable/capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTAP payment basis is operating costs during inpatient stay
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS frames the eligible costs for NTAP as operating costs associated with the technology during the inpatient hospital stay (e.g., Nelli: operating costs of $1,500 for the analysis during inpatient hospital stay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicants include capital and operating components in total cost, CMS will base NTAP on operating costs only; CMS may request more information to determine whether an item is operating vs capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant cost submission and CMS update authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to submit cost information prior to the final rule; CMS notes where applicants have not yet provided estimates and states it 'expects the applicant to submit cost information prior to the final rule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will update and possibly revise the proposed NTAP amounts in the final rule based on revised or additional information it receives before finalizing. Applicants and commenters may supply cost data and CMS may adjust the proposed payment accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for public comment on NTAP proposals and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS repeatedly invites public comments 'on whether [device] meets the cost criterion and our proposal to approve new technology add-on payments' and on 'the use of these ICD-10-PCS procedure codes to identify use of the technology for the Breakthrough Device-designated indication.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address cost criterion, proposed payment amounts, coding lists, eligibility determinations (including Breakthrough indication applicability), capital vs operating cost treatment, and any other factual or policy matters CMS raised; CMS will consider such comments prior to the final rule.
